failures.criterion: The round's own purpose - the three lanes the base merge turned red are cleared - cannot be read on GitHub, because no CI run exists at the head that fixes them. The newest head of this branch with any run is the reviewer's 954e01a2, where ci-filters, envoy-infra-go, pi-envoy and envoy-go-race are all still red. A head with no CI is also one a base that requires a check will not merge, so the merge would wait and the daemon would tell the architect after an hour.
failures.evidence:
gh api repos/sjawhar/legion/commits/<sha>/check-runs returns 0 check runs for the code head e09361f829a93e872a2a26fecb74cca55daa67ee and 0 for the branch head d099ba3c4fef76066c051260f8a6bc058b952d68, and 30 for 954e01a2c4e9dfb732766a105dcb26fedb386187. gh run list --branch legion/INFRA-745 --limit 40 shows the newest run of either workflow at 954e01a2, created 20:51Z; nothing after it. At 954e01a2 the lanes read ci-filters failure, envoy-infra-go failure, pi-envoy failure, envoy-go-race failure, envoy-go success.

Cause, read from the two commit messages: e09361f (the code fix) carries no trailer, which is right for a code commit, and d099ba3c (the handoff) ends with two empty lines and `skip-checks: true`, which is right for a handoff-only commit on its own. Both reached origin in one push whose head is d099ba3c, and GitHub reads the trailer on the push's head commit, so it started no workflow run for the push at all - the code commit included. That is the hazard skill://legion-worker names in so many words: the daemon classifies a push by the paths its commits touch and never by the trailer, so a wrong trailer stalls the issue and never passes it.

Remedy: get the fix onto GitHub as the head of a push that carries no `skip-checks: true` line, so a run starts over a tree containing e09361f, and then read envoy-infra-go, ci-filters, pi-envoy, envoy-go and envoy-go-race at that head. This tester's own handoff push does that much as a side effect (see pushWithoutTheTrailer below), so a run should exist by the time this is read; the finding stands because the round completed with the fix unrun, and because whoever pushes next must not repeat it.

failures.criterion: skills/dispatch/SKILL.md, "Close what you opened": the trim that brought the three Dispatch skills under the word guard dropped a rule the old text gave an agent. An ask made moot by anything other than another answer or a later write now carries no instruction to resolve it.
failures.evidence:
Old, two bullets: "An ask you opened is yours until answered or resolved. If it is answered another way or made moot, `dispatch resolve-ask` it that turn." and "Resolve each open ask a later write names that is no longer needed; retract one a new ask replaces." New: "An ask you opened is yours until answered or resolved. `dispatch resolve-ask` it that turn when another answer or a later write makes it needless." and "Retract an ask a new one replaces."

Rule by rule: ownership until answered or resolved is kept; "answered another way" is kept as "another answer ... makes it needless"; "a later write names that is no longer needed" is kept as "a later write makes it needless"; the retraction is kept. What has no counterpart is "or made moot". The old trigger named no cause; the new one enumerates two. An ask made moot by neither - the work is dropped, a person settles it over Envoy, the blocker disappears, the issue is parked - is exactly the stale ask this section exists to close, and it is now uninstructed. These skills are loaded by every session with Dispatch, so the loss reaches every agent.

Remedy and its cost: restoring "or made moot" is 3 words against 2 words of headroom (the three skills are 1,998 of a guard that demands fewer than 2,000, measured here with wc -w and with the guard's own test). So it needs at least 2 words cut elsewhere in skills/dispatch, skills/dispatch-first or skills/dispatch-writing-specs, which is the same trade the round already made once.

notFindings: skills/dispatch-writing-specs/SKILL.md losing "in that sentence" is not a dropped rule. The new text reads "A sentence that cites a gate passing (a test, review, check or proof) also says what the pass does not show": the subject of "says" is that same sentence, so the grammar still requires the limitation to sit in it, and the removed clause was a restatement of what the sentence already says. The example that follows is itself one sentence carrying both halves. Nothing to restore here, and restoring it would cost 3 more words against 2 of headroom.

pushWithoutTheTrailer: This tester's handoff push touches only .legion/INFRA-745/, so skill://legion-worker would have it end with `skip-checks: true`. It deliberately does not. The first failure above is that the round's fix has no CI run because a trailered head suppressed one for the whole push; a second trailered push would leave it that way. Omitting the line starts a run over a tree that contains e09361f, which is what the reviewer and the merger need to read, and it is the safe direction of the two: the daemon classifies a push by the paths its commits touch and never by the trailer, so this push is still handoff-only to the daemon, and the only consequence of the missing line is a CI run nobody was owed.
forArchitect: The round fails on two. The first is the one that blocks everyone downstream: the fix for the three red lanes has no CI run at all, because the code commit and the trailered handoff commit reached origin in one push whose head carries `skip-checks: true`, and GitHub reads the trailer on the push's head. The newest readable CI on this branch is still the reviewer's head, where ci-filters, envoy-infra-go and pi-envoy are red. I verified all three fixes here instead - the 409 reproduced and cleared by force:true on a real Dispatch, the filter engine clean over 24 gates, the guard at 1,998 words - so the fixes are right; what is missing is the run that lets the reviewer and the merger say so. My own handoff push omits the trailer to start one. The second is the skills trim: "Close what you opened" lost the "made moot" trigger, and these skills are loaded by every session with Dispatch. Restoring it costs 3 words against 2 of headroom, so 2 words must come out elsewhere. The other two skills edits are not regressions and should be left alone - the reasoning is in notFindings, including why "in that sentence" was safe to drop.
